## 0. What this document is, and what it is not

It answers one question per source: **what kinds of opportunity signal could this**
**source expose, if we were permitted to collect from it.**

Three things it is not, each of which it would be easy to mistake it for:

- **Not permission.** A source can cover `entertainment` and be `PROHIBITED`.
  Coverage and eligibility are different tables and no view joins them into one
  verdict. The usability column here is a reminder, never an input.
- **Not evidence weight.** There is no number anywhere in this document. A
  per-source reliability coefficient is D-03, which is blocked, and §35 names the
  exact shape of the mistake: `Reddit = 0.7`.
- **Not a measure of quality.** The counts below count SOURCES. Ten sources
  covering a family is not better evidence than one; it is more places to look.

## 1. The vocabulary

Sixteen signal families and seventeen behaviours. The behaviours are Ontology V2
§3.4 unchanged — Mission 1.7 §5 asked for exactly the canonical list, so no second
behaviour vocabulary was created. Eleven of the sixteen signal families project a
canonical `user_motivation` entry and record which one; five record no projection,
four because none exists and `desire` because its counterpart is a closed enum that
a registry pointer cannot reference.

Column keys, in order: `crea`=create, `play`=play, `comp`=compete, `coll`=collect, `cust`=customize, `shar`=share, `disc`=discuss, `disc`=discover, `lear`=learn, `comp`=compare, `pred`=predict, `cons`=consume, `trac`=track, `buy`=buy, `sell`=sell, `coll`=collaborate, `auto`=automate.

**11 sources record no behaviour at all**: `discord`, `eurostat`, `fred`, `meta-instagram`, `pinterest`, `spotify`, `tiktok`, `twitch`, `world-bank`, `x-twitter`, `youtube`.

Two different reasons, and they are worth separating. The economic sources record
none because aggregate national statistics contain no individual behaviour — that
is a property of the data and not a gap in the review. The rest record none because
their documentation could not be retrieved or the source is `PROHIBITED`, so there
is no basis to cite and nothing may be claimed.

## 4. Coverage by family, counting only what may be used

§23: a `PROHIBITED` source is not coverage, and neither is a `RESTRICTED` one for
this use case. **AVAILABLE** counts sources in an approving state. The other two
columns are what a change of verdict would buy.

| Signal family | AVAILABLE | PENDING | BLOCKED | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `desire` | 0 | 1 | 4 | **UNCOVERED** |
| `entertainment` | 1 | 0 | 3 | partial |
| `creativity` | 0 | 1 | 1 | **UNCOVERED** |
| `curiosity` | 3 | 2 | 0 | **covered** |
| `competition` | 0 | 0 | 1 | **UNCOVERED** |
| `collection` | 0 | 0 | 1 | **UNCOVERED** |
| `personalization` | 0 | 0 | 0 | **UNCOVERED** |
| `status` | 0 | 0 | 0 | **UNCOVERED** |
| `social` | 1 | 2 | 0 | partial |
| `community` | 1 | 3 | 1 | partial |
| `discovery` | 4 | 5 | 1 | **covered** |
| `learning` | 3 | 1 | 0 | **covered** |
| `trend` | 8 | 3 | 5 | **covered** |
| `commercial` | 5 | 2 | 4 | **covered** |
| `developer_activity` | 3 | 3 | 1 | **covered** |
| `problem` | 0 | 4 | 4 | **UNCOVERED** |

**7 of 16 families have no usable source at all**: `desire`, `creativity`, `competition`, `collection`, `personalization`, `status`, `problem`.

**3 rest on a single source**: `entertainment`, `social`, `community`. A family covered by one source is a family covered by one source's biases.

| `collection` | `steam` | verdicts, not capability |

| `problem` | `bluesky`, `hacker-news`, `reddit`, `stack-exchange`, `apple-app-store`, `github`, `google-play`, `steam` | verdicts, not capability |

## 5. Portfolio balance

§40 asks what proportion of source categories are economic rather than
consumer or social. Category counts, not quality claims.

| Source family | Registered | Approving | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|
| `developer` | 4 | 2 | `github`, `huggingface`, `npm-registry`, `pypi` |
| `social` | 4 | 0 | `bluesky`, `meta-instagram`, `tiktok`, `x-twitter` |
| `community` | 3 | 0 | `discord`, `hacker-news`, `reddit` |
| `economic_data` | 3 | 3 | `eurostat`, `fred`, `world-bank` |
| `app_store` | 2 | 0 | `apple-app-store`, `google-play` |
| `content_platform` | 2 | 0 | `spotify`, `youtube` |
| `knowledge` | 2 | 2 | `openalex`, `wikimedia-pageviews` |
| `product_discovery` | 2 | 0 | `pinterest`, `product-hunt` |
| `creator` | 1 | 0 | `twitch` |
| `forum` | 1 | 0 | `stack-exchange` |
| `gaming` | 1 | 0 | `steam` |
| `news` | 1 | 1 | `gdelt` |
| `search_trends` | 1 | 0 | `google-trends` |

**Registered: 3 of 27 sources are economic data (11%), across 13 families.**
**In an approving state: 3 of 8 (37%).**

The registered figure is the healthier of the two and it is the less meaningful
one. What the system may actually collect from is the second, and there the
economic share is far higher than the catalog as a whole suggests — which is the
bias §40 asks to be reported rather than the one it hopes for.
